activity_context.topic_title: Second-Order Homogeneous ODEs: Characteristic Equations With Complex Roots

feedback.problem: Given that $y=y(x)$ satisfies the equation ${y}^{″}+2{y}^{′}+50y=0,$ which of the following is **not** a solution to this equation?
feedback.worked_solution:
Assuming $y={e}^{\lambda x}$ and differentiating $y$ with respect to $x$ gives

$$
{y}^{′}=\lambda {e}^{\lambda x},\,{y}^{″}={\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}.
$$

Substituting the above into our differential equation gives

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}{e}^{\lambda x}+2\lambda {e}^{\lambda x}+50{e}^{\lambda x} & =0 \\ {e}^{\lambda x}({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +50) & =0.\end{aligned}
$$

The auxiliary equation is therefore

$$
{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +50=0.
$$

The auxiliary equation can be solved by completing the square:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +50 & =0 \\ ({\lambda }^{2}+2\lambda +1)-1+50 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2}+49 & =0 \\ (\lambda +1)^{2} & =-49 \\ \lambda +1 & =\pm 7\text{i} \\ \lambda  & =-1\pm 7\text{i}\end{aligned}
$$

Hence, $\lambda =-1\pm 7\text{i}$ are the complex roots of the auxiliary equation.

Thus, any linear combination of the functions $\text{Re}({e}^{(-1+7\text{i})x})={e}^{-x}\operatorname{cos}⁡7x$ and $\text{Im}({e}^{(-1+7\text{i})x})={e}^{-x}\operatorname{sin}⁡7x$ is a solution to the original differential equation. 

Among the given options, only $50{e}^{x}\operatorname{sin}⁡7x$ is not a solution.
